text: The final examination. One crate, in a pen. One door, a long way from it. Everything I own is in between.
You have one crate. Count the things in here that a crate could solve. Then stop expecting me to give you a second crate.
The crate travels ahead of you, twice. Nothing gets carried through that doorway, and nobody should walk through it while anything past it is still looking.
That room is not part of the examination. Nothing in it will be marked. Come out. I cannot invigilate a cupboard.
There is nothing to solve in here. Stand still. Admire the gallery under the observation window, if you must. Do not stand on it.
That sentry's aim has drifted. I would not stand near the glass. What it misses, it breaks. And what is behind the glass was built by people who liked a slot in a wall.
One of my cameras sweeps. The other has not blinked since it was installed. Neither of them can see through a pot plant.
There are three clean panels down here, and the third cannot be seen until you have used the second. I would rather you had not noticed any of them.
The panel in the screen turns round every few seconds, and whatever is on it goes round with it. I am told left and right change places on the way. Nobody ever stayed to check.
Failing is not a waste. What the door wants is kept where the failures were. After that, to come out on the left, start on the right.
That is the holding room. Failed subjects waited there for collection. Collection was every second Thursday. I have lost track of Thursdays.
I am not going to help you with this one. The marks on the walls are not mine. I never found out who made them.
The spark comes out above my door and hits the wall behind you. Each mark faces something that would very much like a spark.
The field takes your portals if you walk through it. Light is not the only thing that can go in at the pillar and come out at the panel.
There is no second hint. There was barely a first one. The door, please.
